findings.title: Update prune.sh to consume the v2 manifest before emitting it
findings.comment: /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/snapshot.sh:114 emits label, epoch, bytes, path; /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/prune.sh:70 still reads epoch, bytes, path. The resulting path contains the byte count and a tab, so the existence check skips it. End-to-end runs for nightly and nightly-prod with BACKUP_KEEP=1 both exited 0 and retained old archives. README explicitly declares v2 consumption; continued v1 parsing does not satisfy that contract. The first-hyphen label bug is pre-existing, but failure to consume the new explicit label is part of this migration defect.

findings.title: Escape values before constructing the remote shell command
findings.comment: /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/lib/common.sh:98 surrounds interpolated values with single quotes but does not escape embedded single quotes. A local SSH stand-in evaluating the actual generated command executed printf INJECTED from a crafted archive basename and returned success. snapshot.sh accepts that label because it only rejects empty labels. Ordinary apostrophes can also change command parsing; local argument quoting does not protect the remote shell.

findings.title: Publish remote archives only after a verified complete transfer
findings.comment: /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/lib/common.sh:98 opens the final remote .tar.gz directly, with neither temporary publication nor cleanup. A stand-in remote cat that wrote eight bytes and returned failure left an eight-byte final-name archive while replicate exited 1. The same redirection also truncates an existing same-name replica before success. This contradicts the explicit partial-transfer guarantee at lines 89–92 and can leave an unusable backup appearing complete.

findings.title: Test the force value explicitly instead of its non-emptiness
findings.comment: /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/snapshot.sh:22 maps unset, empty, and 0 BACKUP_FORCE values to the nonempty string 0. /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/lib/common.sh:81 therefore enables the override during both preflight checks. With df reporting zero available KB, check_free_space / 100 0 returned 0. Reading FORCE before config is explicitly intentional in README; the defect is the truth test, not configuration precedence.

findings.title: Set restrictive permissions on the remote replica
findings.comment: /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/lib/common.sh:14 sets only the local process umask; the SSH command at line 98 does not establish remote permissions. Running the actual generated command with remote umask 022 produced directory mode 0755 and archive mode 0644. On a replica with traversable parent directories, other users can read the backed-up source data, unlike the deliberately private local archives. Redirection also preserves permissive modes on an existing destination.

findings.title: Restore unconditional cleanup after creating the stage
findings.comment: /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/snapshot.sh:90 creates STAGE without replacing the deleted EXIT/INT/TERM cleanup trap; make_stage only creates and prints the directory. The remaining rmdir at line 111 is reached only after tar, replication, and mv succeed. Separately injected failures in all three commands exited 1 and each left a partial or complete archive in TMPDIR. Repeated failed runs therefore accumulate scratch data instead of cleaning it as before.

Audit the free-space gate’s default and override semantics. Follow BACKUP_FORCE and --force through configuration loading and shell truth tests.
Scrutinize the off-host replication boundary for remote-shell quoting, partial-transfer publication, and failure behavior.
Check scratch staging cleanup on every success and failure path. Include failures from tar, SSH, and moving the archive.
Compare the new find-based archive enumeration with the previous glob behavior. Focus on literal labels, symlinked directories and files, unusual filenames, and retention ordering.
